metadata.note: The Augusta Southern line, Augusta - Gracewood - Hephzibah - Blythe - Keysville - Wrens - Stapleton - Avera - Gibson - Mitchell - Warthen - Sandersville - Tennille, Georgia (84.8 mi per Fowler). One line with no branches, split by operator era (Rule 4): the Sandersville and Tennille (1877-1893), the 3-ft-gauge Augusta, Gibson and Sandersville (Augusta - Gibson 1886-1893, Gibson - Sandersville 1887-1893; two features only because the halves opened in different years), the Augusta Southern (1893-1897 and 1901-1919), the South Carolina and Georgia as lessee (1897-1901), and the Georgia and Florida Railway on Keysville - Tennille (1920-1927 [OPEN]). Features in different eras share identical geometry. Augusta - Keysville after 1919 became the G&F's main line into Augusta and is deliberately NOT drawn here: it is deferred to a future Georgia & Florida layer with its own research, so no G&F year is asserted on it.
sources: ICC valuation abstract, Augusta Southern Railroad (Wikipedia WikiProject Trains/ICC valuations/Augusta_Southern_Railroad)
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952, Sandersville Railroad entry (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt line 21987)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The Augusta Southern grade is mapped in OSM under old_railway_operator='Georgia and Florida' (its post-1919 owner): abandoned/razed ways named 'Augusta Southern Railroad' (164908552, 164908638, 1085033702, 1085033703, 164908465, 1085033704, 164908471, 1085033706, 1085033707, 1085033708, 1085033709, 1085033705, and the live NS stub 374854594 at Tennille), road ways built on the grade and carrying the same tag (Stapleton Highway 164908405, Griffin Circle 164908387 and Railroad Avenue 9249856 in Gibson), and the surviving Norfolk Southern 'Moores District' tracks Augusta - Hephzibah (387263295, 387263290, 387243183, 387243176, 387243196 and others; tiger:name_base 'Augusta Beltline Railroad:Georgia and Florida Railway'). The Augusta - Tennille trace ran 78.4 mi on those tagged ways and 0 mi on any other operator, untagged rail, OpenHistoricalMap way or trail, with no straight legs; 0.6 mi of NS Moores District yard track (way 385906819, same tag) was then prepended by hand to carry the line from the trace's start into south downtown Augusta. Old_railway_operator probes: 'Georgia and Florida' matched; 'Augusta Southern' matched only as a name; 'G&F', 'AS' and 'Southern' found nothing on this line ('Southern' matched only the NS R Line north of downtown Augusta, not used). The general railway degree-tiles could not be fetched (every Overpass mirror timed out on them for the whole session), so the graph was built from the operator-tagged ways and the fetch_gap results (OSM abandoned/trail ways and OpenHistoricalMap for Hephzibah - Keysville; the Keysville - Tennille fetch_gap OSM query never completed, so OpenHistoricalMap was queried directly for 32.90,-82.88,33.30,-82.20 and its 21 ways added) only; because the trace never left own-tagged ways this does not affect the line, but it means no competing untagged track was offered to the router. Waypoints (Nominatim, every result checked: all are the named town or CDP, none a county): Gracewood (locality), Hephzibah, Blythe, Keysville, Wrens, Stapleton, Avera, Gibson, Mitchell, Warthen (census place), Sandersville, Tennille; every one lies within 1.1 km of the drawn line. Not used: Mathews (no geocode), De Bruce (geocoded to a street in Atlanta), Silas (geocoded to 'Silas Lane'). The Sandersville - Tennille leg is the AS grade (OSM ways 1085033705/374854594 named 'Augusta Southern Railroad'), NOT the still-active freight-only Sandersville Railroad, which has its own separate alignment: the OSM main API shows the live Sandersville Railroad main (ways 965396407, 965396408, 484518674) running from Tennille north-east to about -82.794, 32.96 and then to Sandersville, while the AS grade (1085033705) runs due north from Tennille west of it. OpenHistoricalMap's unnamed 1889-dated ways 202210156/202210301 follow the Sandersville Railroad's eastern route and were NOT used. OpenHistoricalMap's other ways here (202210305, 202210154, 202210157: Hephzibah - Keysville - Wrens - Sandersville, unnamed, start_date 1889, very coarse) were offered to the router but not taken.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Georgia and Florida Railway, Keysville - Tennille: drawn to 1927, the last confirmed passenger year (Fowler 'b: 1927t' on Haddens); line abandoned 1934; the real passenger end is unknown and may be anywhere 1927-1934. A 'last train' story (Sandersville Progress, Augusta Chronicle, 1933-34) would settle it. (2) Fowler letter reading: the AS section header defines only 'a: 1913 (SOU) t'; the b (1927t) and w (1924w) letters are read from the G&F header directly above. If they apply only to the G&F main line, the 1927 evidence is weaker. (3) Lease conflict 1897-1901: RailGa AS page says SC&G lease 1897, then Southern Railway lease April 1899 - April 1901; RailGa SC&G page and Wikipedia say SC&G lease 1897-1901, then Southern control. Drawn as SC&G 1897-1901; who ran the trains 1899-1901 is open. (4) G&F 'control' about 1918 (Wikipedia) vs purchase Oct 31, 1919: split at 1919; move it a year earlier if the G&F operated the AS from 1918. (5) AG&S passenger starts are collapsed to the first full year after each opening (1886, 1887); passenger use positively evidenced only from 1889 equipment returns. (6) S&T: October 1876 opening not drawn (passenger evidence from 1877). (7) S&T gauge after the 1893 lease (5 ft -> 3 ft -> standard 1895?) inferred, unsourced. (8) Mileage: Fowler 84.8 (from Augusta Union Depot), Official Railway List 1894 84, ICC 81.5 (78.20 + 3.30), RailGa '80-mile' + 3.3. (9) All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; RailGa's 1895 and 1917 AS timetable images were not read. (10) G&F trackage rights Augusta - Keysville from 1906 (RailGa G&F page) or 1910 (RailGa AS page) - matters only to a G&F layer. (11) Augusta Union Depot approach not located; the drawn line stops about 1.4 mi short.
metadata.omitted: Augusta - Keysville under the Georgia & Florida after 1919 (deferred to a G&F layer; no years asserted). Southern Railway lease 1899-1901 as a separate feature (only the RailGa AS page supports it; folded into the SC&G feature with the conflict recorded). The Sandersville Railroad (Sandersville - Tennille, built 1894-95 as the AS's competitor on a separate alignment): freight only from at least Sept 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide), passenger years before that not researched - not drawn, and its track is not used for the S&T/AS geometry.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: No freight-only tail drawn: Keysville - Tennille ends at 1927 [OPEN], not at the 1934 abandonment; Hephzibah - Keysville freight to 1966 and Augusta - Hephzibah under Norfolk Southern today are not drawn as AS or G&F service. The Sandersville Railroad is excluded (freight only per the Feb 1952 Guide).
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: the AG&S and S&T were steam from opening (S&T Porter tank engine documented 1877). Nothing trimmed.

properties.geometry_quality: Sandersville - Tennille (the Sandersville - Tennille part of the AS grade): traced 3.2 mi against a documented 3.3 mi (RailGa S&T page), 3.5 mi (RailGa AS page), 3.30 mi (ICC valuation) and 3.2 mi on Fowler's mileposts (81.6 - 84.8). No straight-line legs added by the tracer: every mile runs on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Georgia and Florida' (the AS grade's later owner). Traced chainage from the drawn Augusta end vs Fowler's mileposts from Augusta Union Depot: Gracewood 7.0/8.4, Hephzibah 13.8/14.9, Blythe 19.1/21.6, Keysville 24.5/26.4, Wrens 34.6/37.7, Stapleton 39.4/42.4, Avera 43.9/47.0, Gibson 48.9/52.2, Mitchell 55.4/60.6, Warthen 66.6/72.2, Sandersville 75.9/81.6, Tennille 79.1/84.8 (town-centre geocodes). This is the Augusta Southern / S&T grade (OSM 'Augusta Southern Railroad' ways), NOT the separate, still-active Sandersville Railroad. QUALITY CAVEATS: (1) AUGUSTA END - the line stops on NS Moores District track at about -81.9697, 33.4607 in south downtown Augusta; the approach to Augusta Union Depot (Fowler's milepost 0) was not located and is NOT drawn, worth roughly 1.4 mi on Fowler's figures (Gracewood 7.0 traced vs 8.4). (2) The Hephzibah - Keysville - Tennille grade is lifted (Hephzibah - Keysville 1966, Keysville - Tennille 1934); OSM maps it as abandoned/razed ways, several of them coarse (way 1085033704, Gibson - Mitchell - Agricola, 25 vertices for 9.9 mi; 1085033705, Sandersville - Tennille, 7 vertices for 2.85 mi; 1085033703 east of Wrens, 6 vertices for 1.6 mi), so curvature is under-drawn there, which is the likeliest cause of the Gibson - Mitchell shortfall (6.5 traced vs 8.4). Long two-vertex tangents in those razed ways may have been approximated by the OSM mapper rather than traced from a surviving grade; they are drawn as OSM has them and listed so the reader can judge: east of Wrens 2.5 mi (1085033703/164908638), Gibson - Mitchell 1.5 mi and 2.1 mi and Mitchell - Agricola 2.3 mi (1085033704), Warthen - Sandersville 1.4 mi (1085033709), Sandersville - Tennille 2.0 mi (1085033705) - 11.8 mi in all, about 15% of the line. About 4.2 mi runs on roads laid on the grade (Stapleton Highway west of Wrens, 3.4 mi; Griffin Circle and Railroad Avenue in Gibson, 0.9 mi) - OSM tags them as the former railway, but a road can straighten a grade. (3) ERA - drawn on the alignment as OSM records it (the standard-gauge road as later owned by the Georgia & Florida, and NS track at the Augusta end). Whether the 1885-1895 3-ft-gauge AG&S, and the 5-ft S&T of 1876, used exactly this alignment was not checked; any line change at the 1895 gauge conversion, and the Augusta terminal trackage of the period, are not represented.

segments.note: Sandersville and Tennille Railroad, a short steam shuttle from Sandersville to the Central of Georgia main line at Tennille. Opened October 1876 (RailGa); 1877 is the first year with positive passenger evidence - an 1877 report quoted by RailGa says its Porter tank engine 'hauled two baggage/passenger cars' (5-ft gauge, 48-lb rail, 13 mph usual speed); 1889: 1 locomotive, 2 cars. Late 1876 is very probably passenger too but the source says only 'opened', so it is not drawn. Ends 1893, when the Augusta Southern leased the S&T (bought/consolidated by agreement Feb 13, 1894, per the ICC valuation) - a change of operator, not an end of service; the AS feature carries the line on from 1893. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE (a few trips a day to meet Central of Georgia trains assumed; no S&T timetable checked). Steam from the start - no horsecar era (Rule 5).
sources: Segment-level: start 1877 = first positively evidenced passenger year (1877 report on the RailGa S&T page); end 1893 = AS lease (RailGa S&T and AS pages). Headway NOT sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Augusta, Gibson and Sandersville Railroad, 3-ft narrow gauge, steam. Opened in stages (RailGa): Augusta - Stapleton Sept 1885, Stapleton - Avera Oct 1885, Avera - Gibson Dec 10, 1885. Drawn from 1886, the first full calendar year after Gibson was reached (collapsed inward per the research report); passenger service from opening is very probable but only positively evidenced by the 1889 equipment return (4 locomotives, 8 passenger cars, 43 freight/misc cars - RailGa citing Poor's). Conservative alternative if only proven years are wanted: 1889-1893. Ends 1893: receivership, and the road was bought after foreclosure and reorganized as the Augusta Southern effective May 1, 1893 (ICC valuation) - an operator change, not an end of service. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed; no timetable train count was checked - RailGa's 1895 and 1917 AS timetable images were not read).
sources: Segment-level: openings Sept 1885 - Dec 10 1885 (RailGa AG&S page), passenger equipment 1889 (RailGa citing Poor's), end = reorganization as Augusta Southern May 1 1893 (RailGa; Wikipedia; ICC valuation abstract). Start 1886 is an inward collapse, not a sourced first-train year. Headway NOT sourced (estimate).

The Augusta Southern grade is mapped in OSM under old_railway_operator='Georgia and Florida' (its post-1919 owner): abandoned/razed ways named 'Augusta Southern Railroad' (164908552, 164908638, 1085033702, 1085033703, 164908465, 1085033704, 164908471, 1085033706, 1085033707, 1085033708, 1085033709, 1085033705, and the live NS stub 374854594 at Tennille), road ways built on the grade and carrying the same tag (Stapleton Highway 164908405, Griffin Circle 164908387 and Railroad Avenue 9249856 in Gibson), and the surviving Norfolk Southern 'Moores District' tracks Augusta - Hephzibah (387263295, 387263290, 387243183, 387243176, 387243196 and others; tiger:name_base 'Augusta Beltline Railroad:Georgia and Florida Railway'). The Augusta - Tennille trace ran 78.4 mi on those tagged ways and 0 mi on any other operator, untagged rail, OpenHistoricalMap way or trail, with no straight legs; 0.6 mi of NS Moores District yard track (way 385906819, same tag) was then prepended by hand to carry the line from the trace's start into south downtown Augusta. Old_railway_operator probes: 'Georgia and Florida' matched; 'Augusta Southern' matched only as a name; 'G&F', 'AS' and 'Southern' found nothing on this line ('Southern' matched only the NS R Line north of downtown Augusta, not used). The general railway degree-tiles could not be fetched (every Overpass mirror timed out on them for the whole session), so the graph was built from the operator-tagged ways and the fetch_gap results (OSM abandoned/trail ways and OpenHistoricalMap for Hephzibah - Keysville; the Keysville - Tennille fetch_gap OSM query never completed, so OpenHistoricalMap was queried directly for 32.90,-82.88,33.30,-82.20 and its 21 ways added) only; because the trace never left own-tagged ways this does not affect the line, but it means no competing untagged track was offered to the router. Waypoints (Nominatim, every result checked: all are the named town or CDP, none a county): Gracewood (locality), Hephzibah, Blythe, Keysville, Wrens, Stapleton, Avera, Gibson, Mitchell, Warthen (census place), Sandersville, Tennille; every one lies within 1.1 km of the drawn line. Not used: Mathews (no geocode), De Bruce (geocoded to a street in Atlanta), Silas (geocoded to 'Silas Lane'). The Sandersville - Tennille leg is the AS grade (OSM ways 1085033705/374854594 named 'Augusta Southern Railroad'), NOT the still-active freight-only Sandersville Railroad, which has its own separate alignment: the OSM main API shows the live Sandersville Railroad main (ways 965396407, 965396408, 484518674) running from Tennille north-east to about -82.794, 32.96 and then to Sandersville, while the AS grade (1085033705) runs due north from Tennille west of it. OpenHistoricalMap's unnamed 1889-dated ways 202210156/202210301 follow the Sandersville Railroad's eastern route and were NOT used. OpenHistoricalMap's other ways here (202210305, 202210154, 202210157: Hephzibah - Keysville - Wrens - Sandersville, unnamed, start_date 1889, very coarse) were offered to the router but not taken.
properties.geometry_quality: Augusta - Tennille: traced 79.1 mi against a documented 84.8 mi (Fowler, from Augusta Union Depot), 84 mi (1894 Official Railway List, per RailGa), 81.5 mi (ICC valuation: 78.20 mi ex-AG&S + 3.30 mi ex-S&T) and about 83 mi (RailGa's '80-mile' Augusta - Sandersville + 3.3 mi). No straight-line legs added by the tracer: every mile runs on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Georgia and Florida' (the AS grade's later owner). Traced chainage from the drawn Augusta end vs Fowler's mileposts from Augusta Union Depot: Gracewood 7.0/8.4, Hephzibah 13.8/14.9, Blythe 19.1/21.6, Keysville 24.5/26.4, Wrens 34.6/37.7, Stapleton 39.4/42.4, Avera 43.9/47.0, Gibson 48.9/52.2, Mitchell 55.4/60.6, Warthen 66.6/72.2, Sandersville 75.9/81.6, Tennille 79.1/84.8 (town-centre geocodes). QUALITY CAVEATS: (1) AUGUSTA END - the line stops on NS Moores District track at about -81.9697, 33.4607 in south downtown Augusta; the approach to Augusta Union Depot (Fowler's milepost 0) was not located and is NOT drawn, worth roughly 1.4 mi on Fowler's figures (Gracewood 7.0 traced vs 8.4). (2) The Hephzibah - Keysville - Tennille grade is lifted (Hephzibah - Keysville 1966, Keysville - Tennille 1934); OSM maps it as abandoned/razed ways, several of them coarse (way 1085033704, Gibson - Mitchell - Agricola, 25 vertices for 9.9 mi; 1085033705, Sandersville - Tennille, 7 vertices for 2.85 mi; 1085033703 east of Wrens, 6 vertices for 1.6 mi), so curvature is under-drawn there, which is the likeliest cause of the Gibson - Mitchell shortfall (6.5 traced vs 8.4). Long two-vertex tangents in those razed ways may have been approximated by the OSM mapper rather than traced from a surviving grade; they are drawn as OSM has them and listed so the reader can judge: east of Wrens 2.5 mi (1085033703/164908638), Gibson - Mitchell 1.5 mi and 2.1 mi and Mitchell - Agricola 2.3 mi (1085033704), Warthen - Sandersville 1.4 mi (1085033709), Sandersville - Tennille 2.0 mi (1085033705) - 11.8 mi in all, about 15% of the line. About 4.2 mi runs on roads laid on the grade (Stapleton Highway west of Wrens, 3.4 mi; Griffin Circle and Railroad Avenue in Gibson, 0.9 mi) - OSM tags them as the former railway, but a road can straighten a grade. (3) ERA - drawn on the alignment as OSM records it (the standard-gauge road as later owned by the Georgia & Florida, and NS track at the Augusta end). Whether the 1885-1895 3-ft-gauge AG&S, and the 5-ft S&T of 1876, used exactly this alignment was not checked; any line change at the 1895 gauge conversion, and the Augusta terminal trackage of the period, are not represented.

segments.note: Augusta Southern Railroad, own operation. Incorporated Apr 4, 1893; bought the AG&S after foreclosure effective May 1, 1893 (ICC valuation abstract) and leased the Sandersville & Tennille in 1893 (consolidated Feb 13, 1894), so Augusta - Sandersville - Tennille was one AS line from 1893. 1894: 84 mi of 3-ft gauge, 4 locomotives, 8 passenger cars (Official Railway List, via RailGa). Converted to standard gauge September 1895. Ends 1897, when the line was leased to the South Carolina & Georgia Railroad, which ran the trains 1897-1901 (separate feature). The S&T, 5-ft in 1877, is apparently counted as 3-ft in the 1894 return - an inference, unsourced. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed; no timetable train count was checked - RailGa's 1895 and 1917 AS timetable images were not read).
sources: Segment-level: start = reorganization May 1 1893 (RailGa AS page; Wikipedia; ICC valuation abstract via Wikipedia WikiProject Trains); end = SC&G lease 1897 (RailGa AS and SC&G pages; Wikipedia). Headway NOT sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Augusta Southern Railroad again operating its own trains after the lease ended in April 1901 (RailGa AS page; Wikipedia has the Southern Railway taking 'control' in 1901). Southern Railway held stock control from 1901, but stock control does not change who ran the trains, so this stays Augusta Southern (Rule 4 tracks the operator). Positive passenger evidence: Fowler's AS section is lettered 'a: 1913 (SOU) t' - a 1913 Southern public timetable lists AS stations (Neco, Elwood, Padgett, Gilmore etc.); RailGa also holds a 1917 AS timetable (image, not read). Georgia & Florida trains also used Augusta - Keysville under trackage rights from 1906 (RailGa G&F page) or 1910 (RailGa AS page) - not drawn here. The G&F took stock control about 1918 (Wikipedia) and bought the property Oct 31, 1919; ends 1919 at that purchase. If the G&F in fact operated the AS from 1918, the split belongs a year earlier (see metadata.not_yet_sourced). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed; no timetable train count was checked - RailGa's 1895 and 1917 AS timetable images were not read).
sources: Segment-level: start = end of lease April 1901 (RailGa AS page); 1913 passenger service evidenced by Fowler's 'a: 1913 (SOU) t' letters; end = Georgia & Florida purchase Oct 31 1919 (RailGa AS and G&F pages; Wikipedia). Headway NOT sourced (estimate).

segments.note: South Carolina and Georgia Railroad ('The Charleston Line') as lessee of the Augusta Southern, running the trains Augusta - Sandersville - Tennille. Lease began 1897 (month not found). SOURCE CONFLICT on the end: the RailGa SC&G page and Wikipedia have the SC&G lease running 1897-1901, then Southern Railway control; the RailGa AS page instead says the Southern Railway leased the AS from April 1899 to April 1901. Drawn to 1901 on the two agreeing sources; the SC&G itself came under Southern Railway control in 1899, so the practical operator 1899-1901 may have been the Southern either way. Recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced, unresolved. Passenger service under the lease is assumed continuous from the AS years either side (positively evidenced 1894 and 1913), not separately sourced. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed; no timetable train count was checked - RailGa's 1895 and 1917 AS timetable images were not read).
sources: Segment-level: lease 1897-1901 per RailGa SC&G page and Wikipedia; conflicts with RailGa AS page (Southern lease Apr 1899 - Apr 1901) - unresolved. No timetable for 1897-1901 checked. Headway NOT sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Georgia and Florida Railway (renamed Georgia and Florida Railroad in the 1926 reorganization - same operator) running the ex-Augusta Southern line west from its own main line at Keysville through Wrens, Stapleton, Gibson, Mitchell, Warthen and Sandersville to Tennille. The G&F bought the AS Oct 31, 1919, so 1920 is its first full year. [OPEN] END: 1927 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end - Fowler's G&F letter 'b' (1927 public timetable) on Haddens [Bealls/Belle Springs], milepost 56.6 between Gibson and Mitchell; 'w' (1924 working timetable) also appears on Rock Comfort 49.0 and Kenmore 54.0. The Keysville - Tennille line was ABANDONED in 1934; that is an abandonment year, not a passenger end, and passengers may have stopped earlier (for example at the 1927-29 Augusta - Greenwood extension or in the 1929-32 Depression cuts). No source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Augusta - Keysville under the G&F after 1919 is deliberately NOT drawn in this layer (deferred to a Georgia & Florida layer). This is the 1906 Georgia & Florida Railway, unrelated to the 1850s 'Georgia and Florida Railroad (predecessor)' of the South Western layer. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one train each way a day assumed).
sources: Segment-level: start = G&F purchase Oct 31 1919 (RailGa G&F and AS pages); end 1927 [OPEN] = Fowler's 'b: 1927t' letter on Haddens (the reading of b/w from the G&F header directly above the AS section is the researcher's - see metadata.not_yet_sourced). Abandonment 1934 (RailGa). Headway NOT sourced (estimate).
